label: Manteiga de garrafa
note: Cooked from cream, not from butter

about.text: A liquid or pasty butterfat from north-east Brazil, made by cooking cream until almost all its water has gone, then decanting and bottling the fat. Brazilian law calls it manteiga da terra, manteiga de garrafa or manteiga do sertao.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.label: cook the cream down
how.text: Cream is boiled down at 110-120 °C until nearly all the water has gone and the milk solids brown and sink. The golden fat is poured off, filtered and sold in a bottle, so it is closer to ghee made straight from cream than to clarified butter.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: The cream is boiled down until bubbling stops and the non-fat solids settle as dense, coffee-brown dregs (borra).

steps.name: decant
steps.note: The clear oily layer is decanted at room temperature.
